top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises a sharply defined invention with a two-name allocation that follows the concept and its decisive realisation: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice, which cancels the lattice light shift so many neutral atoms can be interrogated at once, and Ye's realisation at the 10^-18 level. It is mature, reproduced with Sr, Yb and Hg and checked in clock comparisons, and already used for constants tests, dark-matter searches and millimetre-scale redshift. With the citation confined to the lattice architecture and the 10^-18 regime, it does not overlap the 2005 comb prize or the 2012 single-ion prize. P002 is a close second, broader in concept but with an unrepaired credit gap (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Zhang deceased); P003 is a real discovery but its pairing mechanism and disorder sensitivity make it early; some award is preferred to none.
recusal_note: Research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder; Hall is not a credited name on P001, but Jun Ye is a Hall-lineage JILA scientist. I have no documented collaboration with Katori or Ye and regard this as a disclosed lineage-level bias, with recusal on P001 left to the chair and committee. Lund atomic-physics and quantum-information work lies near B008 and B033, which are not on the slate.
